ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: GPT-5.6 launch stumbles on UX, OpenAI scrambles with fixes days later.
insights: **ChatGPT Work / Codex split** confused users badly enough to trigger emergency usage-limit resets and UI patches
Cloud Work conversations don't sync with desktop Work, threads and local files stay siloed per device
Despite the mess, GPT-5.6 ties **Claude Fable 5** in Code Arena Frontend at roughly half the cost
ai.for_you: Watch how OpenAI handles this correction cycle, it's a live case study in shipping fast then fixing UX in public, relevant if you ever ship agency tools with rough edges to PT SMB clients who won't forgive confusion the way power users will.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most-covered story across every AI source today, and the UX failure is the actually useful signal, not the model itself

ai.name: Anthropic
ai.hook: New 'Jacobian lens' shows Claude visibly puzzling over concepts mid-task.
insights: Tool gives the **clearest interpretability glimpse yet** into what happens inside an LLM during a task, not just at output
Findings range from mundane reasoning patterns to genuinely **unnerving behaviors** researchers didn't expect
Comes right as harness engineering (see Lilian Weng roundup) becomes the dominant framing for agent capability, not raw model size
ai.for_you: No direct build action, but worth 10 minutes: understanding what's actually happening inside these models when they reason helps you debug weird agent behavior in your own agency stack instead of just prompt-guessing.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Genuine research news, not another model launch, and it explains the deeper trend (harness > raw IQ) other sources are pointing at

ai.name: Lilian Weng
ai.role: AI Researcher · via Latent Space / smol.ai
ai.hook: 35 papers distilled into one idea: the agent 'harness' is now the bottleneck.
insights: **Harness engineering** (how you scaffold, retry, and constrain an agent) matters more than swapping in a bigger model
LangChain responded fast with a new **Deep Agents course** and open-source project riding the same framing
Google's Gemini API Managed Agents shipped background execution and custom function calling in the same window
ai.for_you: This directly validates your agency positioning: PT SMBs don't need the fanciest model, they need a well-built harness around whatever model you pick. Worth reading the actual roundup before your next client scoping call.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: The single most actionable conceptual insight across five days of 'not much happened' newsletters

ai.name: xAI
ai.hook: Grok 4.5 ships as a 1.5T-param coding model, priced for volume not benchmarks.
insights: **3x larger** than Grok 4.3, but Musk pitches it on cost-per-token efficiency, not raw score
Priced at **$2/1M input, $6/1M output** with cache discounts, context window returning to 1M tokens soon
Cursor co-trained the model and calls it their most powerful yet, tightening the Cursor-xAI relationship
ai.for_you: Already on your radar from Thursday, but the Cursor partnership detail is new context: if you're picking a coding assistant stack for client work, Cursor + Grok 4.5 is becoming a real alternative to the Anthropic/OpenAI default.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Follow-up detail (Cursor partnership) makes this worth a second mention beyond the initial launch

ai.name: GLM-5.2
ai.hook: Open-source agents just crossed a capability threshold worth tracking.
insights: Nathan Lambert calls it a genuine **step change**, not incremental, after months of monitoring the open ecosystem
Competes directly with Tencent's Hy3 (295B MoE, 21B active params) in the open-weight agent space
Signals open models are closing the agentic gap with frontier closed labs faster than expected
ai.for_you: If cost is a real constraint for PT SMB clients, GLM-5.2 or Hy3 self-hosted via vLLM could undercut API costs for repetitive agency workflows, worth a weekend benchmark against whatever you're currently paying per token.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Interconnects is the most credible open-model tracker in the sources, and this is the strongest claim he's made in months

ai.name: Craig Mod
ai.hook: Rebuilt his own newsletter tool with AI, cut $7K/year to $150.
insights: Replaced Campaign Monitor entirely by building a custom tool with AI assistance
Calls this the start of a **'golden age of tool building'**, anyone can now build software fit to their exact need
Still refuses to let AI write his actual prose, draws a hard line between tool-building and voice
ai.for_you: This is your micro-SaaS thesis in one sentence: bespoke tools replacing $X,000/year SaaS subscriptions for solo creators. Worth listening to the full episode for the build process, not just the outcome, since it's the exact pattern you'd pitch to a PT SMB client paying too much for generic software.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most concretely relevant story to Pedro's actual businesses, repeated across two days of sources because it's genuinely good

build_this.name: Ghost Font
build_this.what_it_is: A font designed to be readable by humans but unreadable/unparseable by AI text extraction.
build_this.why_try_it: Worth a quick look for the yoga platform if you ever want to protect proprietary written content (course scripts, curriculum text) from being scraped and repackaged by AI competitors, though check the actual robustness claims before relying on it.

build_this.name: An agent in 100 lines of Lisp
build_this.what_it_is: A minimal working AI agent implementation stripped down to its essential loop, no framework bloat.
build_this.why_try_it: Read this before your next agency client scoping call, it's the clearest possible mental model of what an 'agent' actually is under the hood, useful for explaining to non-technical PT SMB owners what you're actually selling them without hand-waving.

build_this.name: Mesh LLM (iroh)
build_this.what_it_is: Distributed AI computing framework letting multiple machines share inference load over a peer network.
build_this.why_try_it: Overkill for most agency work today, but worth a bookmark if a future micro-SaaS idea needs cheap distributed inference without renting cloud GPUs, file for later rather than this week.

podcasts.episode: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice
podcasts.takeaway: Craig Mod proves solo creators can now replace expensive SaaS with self-built AI tools for a fraction of the cost.
key_points: Cut newsletter tooling costs from **$7,000/year to $150** by rebuilding Campaign Monitor's function himself
Built a private Twitter alternative for his own paid members called **The Good Place**
Keeps a tech-free morning ritual and refuses to let AI write his actual prose, uses it strictly as research assistant and builder
podcasts.for_you: This is almost a template for what you could pitch PT SMBs paying for bloated SaaS they use 10% of: rebuild the one feature they actually need, cheaper and custom, exactly the agency angle you're already pursuing.

video.title: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice

podcasts.takeaway: Booking.com's CEO says even a dominant travel platform has no durable competitive moat against AI disruption.

podcasts.for_you: No direct action for the agency, but useful framing for client conversations: if a company as entrenched as Booking sees its moat eroding, PT SMBs with weaker digital moats should be more, not less, open to your AI offering.
